newsitem.title: UK: Britain's Cook promises new era in foreign policy.
newsitem.headline: Britain's Cook promises new era in foreign policy.

text.p: Robin Cook, foreign secretary in Britain's new Labour government, promised a fresh start in foreign policy on Sunday and said he wanted human rights and the environment to be at the centre of relations with Europe.

In an interview with the Observer newspaper, Cook said his government wanted to make Britain a leading player in Europe through "constructive engagement" and to make trade and economic cooperation the chief concerns of British embassies.
"We want to take Britain out of a position of isolationism, out of inward-looking chauvinism and into being a leading member of an international community," Cook said.
Ministers, rather than civil servants, will attend all future talks on European integration and Britain would sign the Social Chapter on workers' rights within six weeks.
Labour swept into power at Thursday's election with a majority of 179 in the 659-seat parliament.
Cook repeated the Labour view it was unlikely Britain would join the first wave of those entering a European single currency, due to begin in 1999.
Cook has a busy year ahead, starting next month.

The European Union holds a vital summit in Amsterdam in June to discuss the future of the bloc. Heads of government from British Commonwealth countries meet in Edinburgh in October. Britain is president of the European Union and chairman of the Group of Seven in the first half of 1998.
Cook promised Britain would immediately implement a ban on British sales of landmines and would publish an annual report on British strategic exports, including defence equipment.
